opening.text: Some people leave the porch light on all night. It says someone is home and you are welcome.
God’s love is like that. The light stays on, even when we are far down the road. Today I want to talk about the love of God.

mainMessage.text: God loves each of us fully and always. He sent His Son to show us. We can feel His love, it never runs out, and it changes how we treat other people.

blocks.text: He loves you as His child.
God sent His Son because of His love. We matter to Him because we are His children.
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him. Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf of the First Presidency said this in his talk “The Love of God” from the October 2009 general conference.
We are important to God not because of our résumé but because we are His children.
Our worth is settled.
Nothing can cut the line.
Paul was sure that nothing can separate us from God’s love. Isaiah wrote that God does not forget us.

For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee. Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf of the First Presidency said this in his talk “The Love of God” from the October 2009 general conference.
He loves every one of us, even those who are flawed, rejected, awkward, sorrowful, or broken.
His love does not depend on our best days.
You can feel it.
Nephi called the love of God the most desirable thing of all. Alma gave thanks that God is mindful of every people.

And the angel said unto me: Behold the Lamb of God, yea, even the Son of the Eternal Father! Knowest thou the meaning of the tree which thy father saw? And I answered him, saying: Yea, it is the love of God, which sheddeth itself abroad in the hearts of the children of men; wherefore, it is the most desirable above all things. And he spake unto me, saying: Yea, and the most joyous to the soul.

Now my brethren, we see that God is mindful of every people, whatsoever land they may be in; yea, he numbereth his people, and his bowels of mercy are over all the earth. Now this is my joy, and my great thanksgiving; yea, and I will give thanks unto my God forever. Amen.
Elder Paul E. Koelliker of the Seventy said this in his talk “He Truly Loves Us” from the April 2012 general conference.
The feeling of love from our Heavenly Father is like a gravitational pull from heaven.
That pull is a sign that He is near.
It does not run out.
The Lord said He loves us with an everlasting love. His mercy toward us is as great as the height of heaven.
The Lord hath appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee.

For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is his mercy toward them that fear him. As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us. Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “Divine Love” in the February 2003 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.
Divine love is perfect, infinite, enduring, and universal.
His love has no expiration date.
Love that helps you grow.
A loving parent corrects. God does too. And He invites everyone to come to Him.
For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.

He doeth not anything save it be for the benefit of the world; for he loveth the world, even that he layeth down his own life that he may draw all men unto him. Wherefore, he commandeth none that they shall not partake of his salvation.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf of the First Presidency said this in his talk “The Love of God” from the October 2009 general conference.
Though we are incomplete, God loves us completely.
Correction and love go together.
Pass it on.
We love because He loved first. Jesus Christ asked us to love one another as He loved us.
We love him, because he first loved us.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
Elder Paul E. Koelliker of the Seventy said this in his talk “He Truly Loves Us” from the April 2012 general conference.
I am confident that our Heavenly Father’s arms are constantly extended.
His open arms invite ours.

story.title: As a hen gathers her chickens

blocks.text: The Savior spoke to the people of Jerusalem with deep feeling.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
He wanted to gather them, as a hen gathers her chicks. Many would not come. The love was never in question. The choice was theirs. His arms are still open.

story.title: Thy right hand shall hold me

blocks.text: David asked where he could ever go to get away from God.

Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence? If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there. If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea; Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me.
David found no place where God’s love could not reach him. If we feel lost, the light is still on, and His hand is still reaching.

Honest words from a parent.
Good letters from home are honest. A parent says what we need to hear. God does too. He does it to draw us in, not push us away.
For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.

He doeth not anything save it be for the benefit of the world; for he loveth the world, even that he layeth down his own life that he may draw all men unto him. Wherefore, he commandeth none that they shall not partake of his salvation.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf of the First Presidency said this in his talk “The Love of God” from the October 2009 general conference.
Though we are incomplete, God loves us completely.
Honest words and deep love go together.
Write back.
When you get a loving letter, you write back. We answer God by loving Him and by loving others. Jesus Christ asked us to love as He loves.
We love him, because he first loved us.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
Elder Paul E. Koelliker of the Seventy said this in his talk “He Truly Loves Us” from the April 2012 general conference.
I am confident that our Heavenly Father’s arms are constantly extended.
Our reply can be a kind act today.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time they answered God’s love with love. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Lovest thou me?

blocks.text: Peter had let the Savior down. After the Resurrection, Jesus Christ spoke with him by the sea.

So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs. He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep. He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
The Savior did not scold Peter. He asked about love, and then gave him work to do. Love brought Peter back. Jesus Christ still trusts us with the people He loves.

application.text: First, read one verse about God’s love each day this week. Second, write a short reply to God in your journal. Third, show His love to one person by helping or listening.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God writes to us in love. I know His love never expires. I know that Jesus Christ is the greatest proof of it. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

blessings: His love will become more real to you.
You will feel closer to Him.
Someone will feel that love through you.

closingVerse.text:
If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
